research_basis.authoring_method: Original synthesis using the user brief and the THE DMI implementation reference as the structural benchmark.
research_basis.licence_handling: Original implementation content informed by Jisc AI maturity structure. Scenarios and practitioner language are independently written to avoid reproducing Jisc wording.

objects.key_discriminator: In AI Strategy & Leadership, The key shift is from scattered AI experimentation to coordinated development with support, governance, and scalable workflows.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: Pilot activity can hide the absence of shared priorities, support, or controls.
Buying tools is not the same as building operational capability around them.

minimum_threshold_evidence: The institution has named ownership, repeatable processes, and support for real use cases.
Governance or risk checks are applied before or during rollout, not only after issues occur.
strong_threshold_evidence: Multiple functions use AI through managed workflows rather than informal workarounds.
Capability building and support move in step with adoption.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.

objects.key_discriminator: In AI Strategy & Leadership, The key shift is from coordinated development to embedded maturity where AI is monitored, governed, and improved as part of normal institutional operations.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: Frequent use can still be fragile if governance, data, or monitoring remain immature.
Visible sponsorship is helpful but does not prove embedded operating discipline.

minimum_threshold_evidence: AI-related decisions are integrated into mainstream strategy, operations, and review cycles.
There is evidence of monitoring, lifecycle management, and accountability.
strong_threshold_evidence: The institution adapts AI practice through continuous learning, not one-off implementation phases.
Responsible use is evident in procurement, deployment, support, and evaluation.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.
